00236.label: Continuous oral treatment

medicines.name: Individual anti-sickness / rescue plan
medicines.dose: To be completed by the prescribing team if needed
medicines.timing: As specified in the individual plan; no routine schedule issued here
medicines.note: Source emetogenic category and local policy guide the decision. No medicine, dose or administration order is selected by this draft.

additional_support: Formal pregnancy-prevention programme, nutrition/taste and muscle symptom review. No source-mandated routine CPK interval or automatic supplement prescription.

Vismodegib can cause severe harm to an unborn baby. Women who could become pregnant need the formal pregnancy-prevention programme, including two recommended contraceptive methods (one highly effective method plus a barrier method), unless the agreed alternative is continuous abstinence, during treatment and for 24 months after stopping. Pregnancy tests are supervised before treatment and monthly, even with absent periods. Men must use a condom, with spermicide if available, during sex with a female partner during treatment and for two months afterwards, including after a vasectomy. Report a suspected patient or partner pregnancy immediately. Do not breastfeed or donate blood during treatment or for 24 months afterwards; do not donate semen during treatment or for two months afterwards. Ask the team to explain and document the full programme; this summary does not replace its materials.

Call urgently for blistering or peeling skin, mouth sores with rash or fever, severe muscle pain or weakness, or dark urine. Seek immediate advice about suspected pregnancy or exposure. Report taste change, reduced eating and weight loss early so support can start.
This is not an issued prescription. The clinician and pharmacist must complete and authorise any supportive medicines.

00415.label: Continuous oral treatment

medicines.name: Individual anti-sickness / rescue plan
medicines.dose: To be completed by the prescribing team if needed
medicines.timing: As specified in the individual plan; no routine schedule issued here
medicines.note: Source emetogenic category and local policy guide the decision. No medicine, dose or administration order is selected by this draft.

additional_support: Fever ≥38°C: hold both medicines and contact the team; restarting requires the agreed plan after at least 24 hours symptom-free. Recurrent episodes need their own assessment. Dabrafenib is moderate-to-high emetic risk and trametinib minimal-to-low; the combined plan must reflect both.

Discuss fertility and pregnancy precautions before starting. Use an effective alternative to hormonal contraception during treatment and for two weeks after dabrafenib and 16 weeks after trametinib; dabrafenib can make hormonal contraception less effective. The team must confirm the method and the later applicable end date for the combination. Do not breastfeed during treatment; ask when it is safe to resume. Report a possible pregnancy promptly.

Fever is a particular concern. At 38°C or above, withhold both medicines and contact the oncology team promptly under the written fever plan; recurrent episodes may require action at the first symptoms. Infection and dehydration also need assessment. Restart only when the team tells you. Urgent help is also needed for vision change, severe rash, chest pain, breathlessness, bleeding or severe muscle symptoms.
This is not an issued prescription. The clinician and pharmacist must complete and authorise any supportive medicines.

00563.label: Continuous oral treatment

medicines.name: Individual anti-sickness / rescue plan
medicines.dose: To be completed by the prescribing team if needed
medicines.timing: As specified in the individual plan; no routine schedule issued here
medicines.note: Source emetogenic category and local policy guide the decision. No medicine, dose or administration order is selected by this draft.

additional_support: Assess tumour lysis risk when tumour burden, kidney problems or dehydration raise concern; fluids and additional tests are individual prescriptions. Both oral components are moderate-to-high emetic risk in the source.

Use effective contraception during treatment and for at least one month after the last dose. Hormonal contraception needs an additional or alternative barrier method because interactions can reduce effectiveness. Discuss fertility beforehand and follow the team’s breastfeeding instructions. Report a possible pregnancy promptly.

Contact the team promptly for new visual symptoms, chest pain, breathlessness, palpitations, faintness, severe muscle pain or weakness, dark urine, bleeding, severe rash, persistent diarrhoea or severe abdominal pain. Do not continue one medicine at an unchanged dose if the other has been held without a specific team instruction. Report markedly reduced urine, persistent vomiting, new muscle cramps or weakness, or palpitations promptly; the team may need to check salts, kidney function and tumour lysis risk.
This is not an issued prescription. The clinician and pharmacist must complete and authorise any supportive medicines.

00431.label: Combination induction

medicines.name: Individual low-risk anti-sickness plan
medicines.timing: According to the local low-emetic-risk policy
medicines.note: No routine immune-toxicity steroid or issued prescription is created by this draft.

additional_support: Combination induction is low emetic risk; nivolumab maintenance is minimal risk. Follow the individual/local anti-sickness plan. Routine premedication is not usually required; steroid immune-toxicity rescue is not routine prophylaxis.

Discuss fertility and pregnancy precautions before starting. Immunotherapy may harm a pregnancy. Use the contraception plan and after-treatment duration specified for the medicines you receive; ask about breastfeeding restrictions. Tell the team promptly about possible pregnancy. Do not stop necessary hormone replacement or prescribed steroids without advice.

Immunotherapy can cause inflammation in healthy organs during treatment or after it stops. Contact the oncology team promptly for new diarrhoea, blood in stools, cough or breathlessness, yellow skin or eyes, severe headache, vision changes, marked thirst, unusual weakness or a spreading rash. Tell any clinician that you are receiving or have received immunotherapy.
This is not an issued prescription. The clinician and pharmacist must complete and authorise any supportive medicines.
